## Natural history notes

A large green stink bug characterized by its bright green shield-shaped body, pointed shoulder spines, and pale yellowish margin around the front of the thorax that gives the species its “flavicollis” appearance. In Florida, the Spined Green Stink Bug is found in warm gardens, fields, forest edges, hammocks, parks, roadsides, and shrubby areas where host plants are available. Adults and nymphs feed by piercing plant tissue and drinking sap from leaves, stems, fruits, or seeds, while also serving as prey for birds, spiders, assassin bugs, parasitoid flies, and wasps.
